title: MSF International Managing Director
description: Location: Based in Geneva or within approximately +/- two (2) hours from Geneva Contract: Fixed term at 100% - It is a mandated role (currently 3+3 years) Starting date: 01st of March 2027 Deadline to apply: 26th of November 2026 - We reserve the right to close this position once suitable candidates have been identified. Compensation and Benefits: MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract *By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that. At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics. MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour. We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process. MSF International Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested. I. CONTEXT Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement. Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG). MSF International also provides administrative and operational support to movement-wide initiatives and services, including MSF Access. II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement. The role ensures that MSF International: Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities. Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee); Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care; Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems; Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization; Models MSF values in leadership, equity, duty of care, and ethical management; Ensures that the decisions taken by the Board of Directors of MSF International and its implementation is compliant with the Articles of Association, the internal regulations, as well as Swiss standards and Swiss laws, for as long as the registered office is in Geneva, Switzerland. The MSF Management Director acts as a strategic partner to the International Secretary General, providing leadership on transversal and institutional topics with regards to the management of MSF International. III. ACCOUNTABILITIES 1. Strategic Leadership and Implementation of MSF International (Multi‑year Plan & SPARC): Lead the translation of MSF International and movement strategic priorities into clear objectives, organisational plans, policies and resourcing within MSF International; support cross‑functional initiatives required by international platforms as needed to deliver the Multi‑Year Strategic Plan and SPARC commitments. Expected result: MSF International delivers on agreed strategic priorities and SPARC commitments through coherent plans, measurable milestones and coordinated delivery across functions and movement partners. a. Contribute to the development of MSF International Multi‑year Strategic Plan and SPARC within MSF International’s mandate and scope and translate strategic priorities into concrete organisational objectives, policies, systems and resource allocations, ensuring coherence across functions and services. b. Supports cross‑functional and transversal initiatives required to deliver common strategic priorities and SPARC‑related commitments. c. Contribute to movement-wide discussions on harmonization, efficiency and shared services. d. Sets up and tracks implementation plans, including key milestones, indicators, and risks. Support the ISG in reporting to the International Board and relevant Standing Committees, and contribute to SPARC’s Monitoring & Evaluation Framework and Expense Steering Process for functions and services managed within MSF International’s scope. e. Deputize for the ISG as required, within agreed scope and representation mandates. f. Represent MSF International to key stakeholders, partners and external audiences as required, and build relationships that protect and advance MSF's institutional interests. 2. Governance, legal compliance, accountability and risk management for MSF-International: Ensure robust governance implementation, statutory compliance and effective risk management systems for MSF International as a Swiss legal entity and for services delivered on behalf of the movement; prepare governance-level advice and support Board decision-making. Expected result: International Board and executive decisions are supported by timely, compliant and risk‑informed advice; MSF International statutory obligations and legal requirements are met and organisational risks are identified and mitigated. a. Act as senior management liaison to the ISG, the International Board and Standing Committees on matters related to MSF International organisational governance, resources, risk, compliance and organisational performance. b. Ensure robust systems of internal control, risk management and accountability, are in place and functioning for MSF International, in line with legal, fiduciary and associative obligations, including preparedness for critical incidents directly affecting MSF International. c. Lead or support organizational responses to critical incidents directly affecting MSF International, including HR, legal, reputational, safeguarding or security‑related situations. d. Ensure that MSF International fulfils its statutory responsibilities as a Swiss legal entity and that appropriate legal, administrative and governance support is obtained for decisions of the IB in light of the International Statutes, the Internal Regulations, and Swiss standards and law. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding daily management of MSF International. e. Oversee compliance with GDPR and Swiss data protection law, promoting a culture of privacy and responsible data use. f. Ensure appropriate legal review of all contracts and agreements directly involving MSF International and including those through which it delivers services to the movement, in accordance with MSF’s rules and policies, as well as Swiss law. g. Design, implement and monitor the effectiveness of internal control systems and procedures; ensure that MSF International risks are identified and registered and ensure that mitigation measures are discussed and incorporated in the respective departments annual plans. 3. Services to MSF: Provide executive stewardship of movement-wide services mandated to MSF International, ensuring clear service governance, defined accountabilities and cost‑effective delivery. Expected result: Movement services operate to agreed service charters and KPIs, with transparent costs and reliable delivery that meet sections' needs and contractual obligations. a. Provide executive leadership and stewardship over services mandated to MSF International in support of the MSF movement, ensuring they are clearly governed, fit for purpose, cost‑effective and appropriately funded. b. Ensure that roles, responsibilities, decision‑making authority and service boundaries between MSF International and MSF sections are clearly defined and communicated, balancing interoperability and mutualization objectives with the sections and ODs autonomy. c. Establish and monitor service governance and performance frameworks, including service charters, KPIs, cost‑sharing arrangements and escalation mechanisms where relevant, and ensure transparency. d. Facilitate structured dialogue with MSF sections to identify service needs, manage expectations and address risks or performance issues. 4. Financial stewardship and institutional integrity: Oversee budgeting, financial planning, statutory accounts, audits and financial controls; ensure alignment of resources with strategic priorities and manage institutional financial and insurance arrangements. Expected result: MSF International maintains sound financial health, regulatory compliance and transparent resource allocation that supports strategic objectives. a. Provide executive oversight of budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting for MSF International. b. Ensure alignment between strategic priorities (including SPARC) and resource allocation. c. Oversee statutory accounts, audits, financial policies and compliance with Swiss GAAP, tax and VAT requirements. d. Oversee relationships with external auditors, financial advisors and legal counsel. e. Oversee institutional insurance coverage and financial risk mitigation. Manage the full suite of institutional and corporate insurance coverage for MSF International. f. Oversee legacies and donations earmarked for MSF International 5. People, culture and organisational development: Oversee people strategy, workforce planning, performance management, leadership development and organisational design to foster an inclusive, safe and high‑performing culture across a distributed workforce. Expected result: A diverse, supported and capable organisation with clear succession pathways, strong performance management and a positive organisational culture. a. Provide strategic leadership over human resources management, organizational design and workforce planning. b. Ensure a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. c. Oversee performance management, leadership development and succession planning. d. Ensure a lively MSF International culture despite the geographical spread, including through adequate internal communication. e. Lead organisational development, when necessary, to ensure the organisational structure remains fit for purpose and appropriate for a well-functioning office. f. Manage institutional relationships with MSF sections hosting MSF International staff and ensure coherent frameworks for hosting, contracting, payroll and staff integration. g. Ensure appropriate information governance and that knowledge management systems support collaboration, institutional memory and organizational learning, including learning from strategy and SPARC implementation. h. Liaise regularly with the Staff Committee of MSF International. IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY The MSF International Managing Director operates with a high degree of autonomy to think, interpret and act within the strategic direction set by the International Secretary General, the International Board and the governance framework of MSF International. The role is required to make independent judgements on organisational priorities, resource allocation, risk mitigation, service performance, people matters and operational responses, often in situations where issues are sensitive, cross-functional and without straightforward precedent. The complexity of the environment is significant: the postholder works across a federated MSF movement with multiple stakeholders, distributed teams, hosted staff arrangements and diverse section interests, while also ensuring compliance with Swiss legal and regulatory requirements, internal governance rules, financial and HR procedures, safeguarding standards and data protection obligations. Success therefore depends on balancing institutional coherence, legal and procedural rigour, and service effectiveness with diplomacy, sound judgement and the ability to operate in ambiguity. V. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others. Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels. Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities with respect to required behaviour and report abuse while working for MSF by reinforcing and regularly discussing expected standards of behaviour. Welcome complainants, understand how to guide colleagues to appropriate channels, promote and create an environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour. Guide colleagues to the correct process without investigating. Ensure that staff know how to complain and keep staff updated on reporting mechanisms. Education Master’s degree in management, humanitarian affairs, political sciences, or a related field, or equivalent senior-level professional experience Experience Extensive senior leadership experience (General/Executive Director, Deputy Director or Director of a major organizational function) in a complex and large international and decentralised organisations MSF experience is a major asset Proven ability to operate at Board and executive level Strong people leadership, including conflict management and change leadership Solid expertise in financial oversight, governance and organisational systems Experience with equity, diversity and inclusion strategies Knowledge Strong commitment to MSF’s humanitarian principles and associative values. High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential and sensitive matters. Knowledge of Swiss legal, institutional, employment, financial and data protection frameworks is an asset. Familiarity with governance of associations and federated movements is an asset. Proven ability to lead cross-functional and institutional change. Comfortable leading teams across different locations and liaising with stakeholders at all levels. Excellent written and verbal communication, able to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly, concisely, and professionally. High level of discretion, judgement, and emotional intelligence, and the ability to build a strong network across an organisation. Confident decision‑making and the ability to act autonomously as appropriate. Flexible team player, willing to adapt to changes, and confident tackling unfamiliar challenges across multiple domains of knowledge/experience. Languages Excellent English (written and spoken) is essential. French highly desirable, and other MSF languages are further assets. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding and acceptance of these recruitment procedures. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organisation providing emergency assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters, based solely on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity whose membership is composed of all MSF associations. It hosts the International Secretariat, supports the International Board, facilitates coordination across the MSF movement, and provides shared services and initiatives as mandated by the movement.

Within MSF International, the International Office acts as the Secretariat of the International Board (IB) and operates under the direct management of the International Secretary General (ISG). MSF International also provides administrative and operational support to movement-wide initiatives and services, including MSF Access.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The MSF International Managing Director is a senior executive role responsible for institutional leadership, stewardship of resources, and organizational performance of MSF International as a legal entity serving the MSF movement.

The role ensures that MSF International:

  • Effectively implements -within the scope of MSF International - the MSF International Multiyear Plan and SPARC (MSF-wide Strategic Planning, Accountability and Resource Cycle) and supports the International Board and the International Secretary General in their governance roles and responsibilities.

  • Provides high quality, well governed services to the MSF movement, as mandated by the Full ExCom (executive committee);

  • Operates with strong systems of governance, accountability, risk management and duty of care;

  • Has robust, transparent and efficient governance, financial, human, and knowledge systems;

  • Operates as a coherent, inclusive, and accountable internationally distributed organization;

  • Models MSF values in leadership, equity, duty of care, and ethical management;

  • Ensures that the decisions taken by the Board of Directors of MSF International and its implementation is compliant with the Articles of Association, the internal regulations, as well as Swiss standards and Swiss laws, for as long as the registered office is in Geneva, Switzerland.

The MSF Management Director acts as a strategic partner to the International Secretary General, providing leadership on transversal and institutional topics with regards to the management of MSF International.

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

1. Strategic Leadership and Implementation of MSF International (Multi‑year Plan & SPARC): Lead the translation of MSF International and movement strategic priorities into clear objectives, organisational plans, policies and resourcing within MSF International; support cross‑functional initiatives required by international platforms as needed to deliver the Multi‑Year Strategic Plan and SPARC commitments.

Expected result: MSF International delivers on agreed strategic priorities and SPARC commitments through coherent plans, measurable milestones and coordinated delivery across functions and movement partners.

a. Contribute to the development of MSF International Multi‑year Strategic Plan and SPARC within MSF International’s mandate and scope and translate strategic priorities into concrete organisational objectives, policies, systems and resource allocations, ensuring coherence across functions and services.

b. Supports cross‑functional and transversal initiatives required to deliver common strategic priorities and SPARC‑related commitments.

c. Contribute to movement-wide discussions on harmonization, efficiency and shared services.

d. Sets up and tracks implementation plans, including key milestones, indicators, and risks. Support the ISG in reporting to the International Board and relevant Standing Committees, and contribute to SPARC’s Monitoring & Evaluation Framework and Expense Steering Process for functions and services managed within MSF International’s scope.

e. Deputize for the ISG as required, within agreed scope and representation mandates.

f. Represent MSF International to key stakeholders, partners and external audiences as required, and build relationships that protect and advance MSF's institutional interests.

2. Governance, legal compliance, accountability and risk management for MSF-International: Ensure robust governance implementation, statutory compliance and effective risk management systems for MSF International as a Swiss legal entity and for services delivered on behalf of the movement; prepare governance-level advice and support Board decision-making.

Expected result: International Board and executive decisions are supported by timely, compliant and risk‑informed advice; MSF International statutory obligations and legal requirements are met and organisational risks are identified and mitigated.

a. Act as senior management liaison to the ISG, the International Board and Standing Committees on matters related to MSF International organisational governance, resources, risk, compliance and organisational performance.

b. Ensure robust systems of internal control, risk management and accountability, are in place and functioning for MSF International, in line with legal, fiduciary and associative obligations, including preparedness for critical incidents directly affecting MSF International.

c. Lead or support organizational responses to critical incidents directly affecting MSF International, including HR, legal, reputational, safeguarding or security‑related situations.

d. Ensure that MSF International fulfils its statutory responsibilities as a Swiss legal entity and that appropriate legal, administrative and governance support is obtained for decisions of the IB in light of the International Statutes, the Internal Regulations, and Swiss standards and law. Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding daily management of MSF International.

e. Oversee compliance with GDPR and Swiss data protection law, promoting a culture of privacy and responsible data use.

f. Ensure appropriate legal review of all contracts and agreements directly involving MSF International and including those through which it delivers services to the movement, in accordance with MSF’s rules and policies, as well as Swiss law.

g. Design, implement and monitor the effectiveness of internal control systems and procedures; ensure that MSF International risks are identified and registered and ensure that mitigation measures are discussed and incorporated in the respective departments annual plans.

3. Services to MSF: Provide executive stewardship of movement-wide services mandated to MSF International, ensuring clear service governance, defined accountabilities and cost‑effective delivery.

Expected result: Movement services operate to agreed service charters and KPIs, with transparent costs and reliable delivery that meet sections' needs and contractual obligations.

a. Provide executive leadership and stewardship over services mandated to MSF International in support of the MSF movement, ensuring they are clearly governed, fit for purpose, cost‑effective and appropriately funded.

b. Ensure that roles, responsibilities, decision‑making authority and service boundaries between MSF International and MSF sections are clearly defined and communicated, balancing interoperability and mutualization objectives with the sections and ODs autonomy.

c. Establish and monitor service governance and performance frameworks, including service charters, KPIs, cost‑sharing arrangements and escalation mechanisms where relevant, and ensure transparency.

d. Facilitate structured dialogue with MSF sections to identify service needs, manage expectations and address risks or performance issues.

4. Financial stewardship and institutional integrity: Oversee budgeting, financial planning, statutory accounts, audits and financial controls; ensure alignment of resources with strategic priorities and manage institutional financial and insurance arrangements.

Expected result: MSF International maintains sound financial health, regulatory compliance and transparent resource allocation that supports strategic objectives.

a. Provide executive oversight of budgeting, forecasting and financial reporting for MSF International.

b. Ensure alignment between strategic priorities (including SPARC) and resource allocation.

c. Oversee statutory accounts, audits, financial policies and compliance with Swiss GAAP, tax and VAT requirements.

d. Oversee relationships with external auditors, financial advisors and legal counsel.

e. Oversee institutional insurance coverage and financial risk mitigation. Manage the full suite of institutional and corporate insurance coverage for MSF International.

f. Oversee legacies and donations earmarked for MSF International

5. People, culture and organisational development: Oversee people strategy, workforce planning, performance management, leadership development and organisational design to foster an inclusive, safe and high‑performing culture across a distributed workforce.

Expected result: A diverse, supported and capable organisation with clear succession pathways, strong performance management and a positive organisational culture.

a. Provide strategic leadership over human resources management, organizational design and workforce planning.

b. Ensure a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct.

c. Oversee performance management, leadership development and succession planning.

d. Ensure a lively MSF International culture despite the geographical spread, including through adequate internal communication.

e. Lead organisational development, when necessary, to ensure the organisational structure remains fit for purpose and appropriate for a well-functioning office.

f. Manage institutional relationships with MSF sections hosting MSF International staff and ensure coherent frameworks for hosting, contracting, payroll and staff integration.

g. Ensure appropriate information governance and that knowledge management systems support collaboration, institutional memory and organizational learning, including learning from strategy and SPARC implementation.

h. Liaise regularly with the Staff Committee of MSF International.

IV. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY

The MSF International Managing Director operates with a high degree of autonomy to think, interpret and act within the strategic direction set by the International Secretary General, the International Board and the governance framework of MSF International.

The role is required to make independent judgements on organisational priorities, resource allocation, risk mitigation, service performance, people matters and operational responses, often in situations where issues are sensitive, cross-functional and without straightforward precedent.

The complexity of the environment is significant: the postholder works across a federated MSF movement with multiple stakeholders, distributed teams, hosted staff arrangements and diverse section interests, while also ensuring compliance with Swiss legal and regulatory requirements, internal governance rules, financial and HR procedures, safeguarding standards and data protection obligations. Success therefore depends on balancing institutional coherence, legal and procedural rigour, and service effectiveness with diplomacy, sound judgement and the ability to operate in ambiguity.

V. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

  • Ensure respectful management and communication at all levels.

  • Ensure that staff and consultants under their supervision understand their responsibilities with respect to required behaviour and report abuse while working for MSF by reinforcing and regularly discussing expected standards of behaviour.

  • Welcome complainants, understand how to guide colleagues to appropriate channels, promote and create an environment that does not tolerate abuse or inappropriate behaviour. Guide colleagues to the correct process without investigating.

  • Ensure that staff know how to complain and keep staff updated on reporting mechanisms.


Education

  • Master’s degree in management, humanitarian affairs, political sciences, or a related field, or equivalent senior-level professional experience

Experience

  • Extensive senior leadership experience (General/Executive Director, Deputy Director or Director of a major organizational function) in a complex and large international and decentralised organisations

  • MSF experience is a major asset

  • Proven ability to operate at Board and executive level

  • Strong people leadership, including conflict management and change leadership

  • Solid expertise in financial oversight, governance and organisational systems

  • Experience with equity, diversity and inclusion strategies

Knowledge

  • Strong commitment to MSF’s humanitarian principles and associative values.

  • High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential and sensitive matters.

  • Knowledge of Swiss legal, institutional, employment, financial and data protection frameworks is an asset.

  • Familiarity with governance of associations and federated movements is an asset.

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional and institutional change.

  • Comfortable leading teams across different locations and liaising with stakeholders at all levels.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, able to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly, concisely, and professionally.

  • High level of discretion, judgement, and emotional intelligence, and the ability to build a strong network across an organisation.

  • Confident decision‑making and the ability to act autonomously as appropriate.

  • Flexible team player, willing to adapt to changes, and confident tackling unfamiliar challenges across multiple domains of knowledge/experience.

Languages

  • Excellent English (written and spoken) is essential.

  • French highly desirable, and other MSF languages are further assets.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

title: Grafik-Praktikum
description: Suchen Sie abwechslungsreiche Arbeiten in einer leistungsfähigen Marketing- und Kommunikationsagentur. Interessante Projekte für namhafte Kunden und Marken aus der ganzen Schweiz? Eine abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit und spannende Projekte erwarten Sie in einem lebendigen, professionellen Umfeld mit Freiraum für Kreativität und eigenverantwortlichem Handeln. Ab Januar/Februar 2027 haben wir eine offene Praktikumsstelle. Grafik-Praktikum 60 – 100 % (m/w) Sie haben eine fundierte Ausbildung (mit einem anerkannten Abschluss) als Grafiker/in und sind stark im Design, haben das Flair fürs Schöne? Sie möchten gestalten? Und haben auch eine Affinität zu den neuen Medien? Dann freuen wir uns auf Ihre Bewerbung! Nach einer allgemeinen Einführungsphase arbeiten Sie unter fachlicher Anleitung an konkreten Projekten in allen Marketing- und Kommunikationsbereichen (CI/CD, Werbung, Internet, Messen, Promos, u.v.m.) – und dies für viele bekannte Unternehmen und Marken. Sie sind kreativ und empfänglich für schöne Sachen und haben eine entsprechende Berufsausbildung bzw. ein Studium im Grafik-Bereich absolviert und viele (vielleicht noch verborgene) Talente? Dann warten auf Sie eine interessante Arbeitsstelle und viele Herausforderungen in einem dynamischen Unternehmen. Das Aufgabengebiet reicht von CD-/Editorial-Arbeiten, über Promotions-/Werbekampagnen bis hin zu anspruchsvollen Screen-Designarbeiten für die Online-Kommunikation. Sie sind Grafiker/in aus Leidenschaft und lieben schönes (Marken-)Design. Sie haben die Fähigkeit, einheitlich für unterschiedliche Kanäle zu gestalten, unter Berücksichtigung der Brand Identity. Sie bringen dabei eine entsprechende klassische, grafische Ausbildung mit (mit den entsprechenden Diplomen), dazu Berufserfahrung von 2 – 4 Jahren (sonst Berufseinstieg via Praktikum möglich). Sie haben insbesondere Stärken im Layout/Editorial-Design bzw. in der Typografie, sind talentiert in CI-/CD-Aufgaben und haben gleichzeitig ein Flair für Online-Medien. Sie haben ein Gefühl für die stilvolle, zielgruppengerechte Gestaltung, aber auch den Mut für ausgefallene Ideen. Sie haben ein gewinnendes Auftreten. Sie sind kritikfähig und wollen auch immer etwas dazulernen. Ihre Muttersprache ist Deutsch/Schweizerdeutsch. Zusätzliche Kenntnisse in englischer Sprache sind von Vorteil. Das Praktikum ist eine ideale Chance für den Berufseinsteig. Besonders auch für Studienabgänger. Nach dem Praktikum versuchen wir, Sie im Rahmen einer Festanstellung in unser Team zu integrieren. raw.description:
Compliance Officer / MLRO - Switzerland & Liechtenstein

 

About Keyrock

 

Since 2017, Keyrock has been a change-maker in digital assets. We're a global, remote-first team of 180+ people across 40+ nationalities, with hubs in Brussels, London, Paris, New York and Chicago.

We provide liquidity across 80+ centralized and decentralized exchanges - a position cemented by our Series C, led by SC Ventures. Today we run a full spectrum of capital markets businesses across centralized and on-chain venues: market making, high-frequency trading, options, OTC, DeFi trading desks, advisory, and asset management.

We're building toward the agentic investment banking capabilities for the era of digital finance. A proprietary agentic layer runs the mechanics of the market, so our people can focus on the work code cannot do: the deal, the relationship, and the judgement.

 

We're not just envisioning the future of finance - we're building it.

 

Mission statement

We are looking for an experienced and driven Compliance Officer and MLRO for our Switzerland and Liechtenstein based entities. You will join a dynamic and dedicated Group Compliance team, operating as a key member while focusing primarily on our Switzerland and Liechtenstein operational entities. This role offers an exciting opportunity to make a wider impact across the organization by working on broader, group-level projects, allowing you to contribute to the global compliance framework and help grow the group as a whole.

 

Job description

 

  • Ensuring compliance with all relevant laws and regulations applicable to Switzerland and Liechtenstein by developing and implementing the policies and procedures ;

  • Conducting compliance risk assessments and elaborating an annual compliance plan;

  • Developing and implementing a plan of second-line controls and conducting the tests;

  • Assessing future business activities to identify potential compliance risks;

  • Ensuring the firm’s policies and procedures are being communicated effectively to all relevant employees;

  • Ensuring the compliance trainings are effective and up to date;

  • Keeping abreast with regulatory changes and maintaining the policies and procedures up to date;

  • Collaborate with internal departments such as Trading Operations, Finance, Risk management, IT & Security, etc… to integrate compliance requirements into business processes.

  • Being responsible for oversight of Keyrock CH and LI compliance with its AML obligations and acting as a focal point for the firm’s AML activity (MLRO).

  • Carrying out the duties of a MLRO as per the AML/CTF Framework

  • Representing Keyrock CH and LI in all matters of money laundering prevention internally and externally;

  • Serving as a subject matter expert on AML/CTF matters, providing guidance and support to the compliance team and other departments;

  • Conducting regular audits and reviews to ensure compliance with AML/CTF requirements and internal policies

  • Drafting of compliance points of attention and recommendations and assisting the Group Head of Compliance or Group General Counsel (Group level) with management information reports;

 

Background and experience

  • Solid experience as a Compliance officer (2nd line of defense) in a regulated financial institution in Switzerland and/or Liechtenstein, ideally with exposure to MLRO responsibilities or similar

  • Experience in engaging with Swiss and Liechtenstein regulatory authorities;

  • Excellent knowledge of financial regulations such as MiCAR, AML/CTF, market abuse , data privacy;

  • Understanding of the digital assets ecosystem is a major plus;

  • A relevant degree, preferably in business or law, is required;

  • Extensive experience in implementation of monitoring and control processes to support policies and procedures;

  • A compliance qualification for example ACAMS or a Masters in a related field would be an advantage;

 

Our recruitment philosophy

We look for self-aware candidates who bring both the core skills required for the role and a deep alignment with our performance principles. We seek fiercely passionate, mission-driven people who communicate with purpose and practice proactive ownership. The perfect fit? A crypto enthusiast who prioritizes mission over ego, maintains a commercial mindset, and delivers long-term value through pragmatic flexibility.

Our offer

 

  • A competitive salary and benefits package

  • Annual Team Retreats: a yearly offsite dedicated to strategy, celebration of our wins and fun team activities

  • Opportunity to work remotely

  • Fast-paced, highly intellectually stimulating working environment

  • The freedom to create your own entrepreneurial experience by being part of a team of people in search of excellence

 

As an employer we are committed to building a positive and collaborative work environment. We welcome employees of all backgrounds, and hire, reward and promote entirely based on merit and performance.

 

Due to the nature of our business and external requirements, we perform background checks on all potential employees, passing which is a prerequisite to join Keyrock.

This role will focus mainly on the defence context where we are developing software for advanced on-board UAV situational awareness in military applications. Our solutions are aimed to operate with low-cost and widely available sensors and compute. From there, we plan to develop a line-up of interconnected solutions to safeguard European safety. Our team consists of engineers that are passionate about the technology and solutions they develop. The only time most of us are not thinking about the technology is when we are asleep, and sometimes even then. Our team members have a background in different fields such as Aerospace Engineering, Computational Science and Engineering, Robotics and Computer Graphics. Our office is located in the Aerospace Innovation Hub, a start-up hub located on the TU Delft campus in the faculty of Aerospace Engineering. We work closely with top-tier partners, ranging from government agencies and prime contractors to academic research institutes and other start-ups. Designing multi-layer, high-density PCBs from schematic capture through layout and release. Routing high-speed digital buses (PCIe Gen3/Gen4, MIPI CSI/DSI, USB 3.x) with proper impedance control and length matching. Designing DC power systems for onboard UAV compute and sensor platforms that hold up under LiPo battery voltage sag and EMI from motors and ESCs. Setting technical direction for PCB design and bring-up across the hardware team. Owning hardware from prototype through to a field-ready product. Deep experience with multi-layer PCB design and stack-up planning. Proven high-speed digital routing experience: PCIe (Gen3/Gen4), MIPI CSI/DSI, USB 3.x — impedance-controlled, length-matched traces on multi-layer boards. Experience with DC power filtering and EMI mitigation for battery-powered systems with noisy motor/ESC loads. Hands-on PCB bring-up experience: schematic and circuit debugging, bench-level fault-finding, and flashing firmware to validate hardware. Working in an international, world-class team of engineers and entrepreneurs solving real-life problems with amazing technology. Large freedom in how you work and implement solutions, project ownership is incredibly important to us. The opportunity to take technical risks, to implement stuff the 'right' way and to iterate quickly with tight feedback loops. We are innovating, learning is to be expected. Responsibility over the things you build, you are the expert on what you design and bring up. You’ll join the Traffic Control Features team within TomTom’s Automated Driving organization. The team builds the technology that turns real-world observations into reliable map information about traffic signs, traffic lights, stop lines and road markings. 

You’ll work with applied scientists and software engineers to develop algorithms and machine-learning solutions that detect, position and connect these features to the right roads and driving directions. The goal is to deliver accurate, scalable map content that supports navigation and advanced driving experiences. TomTom measures these features using quality dimensions such as recall, precision, and road-relation accuracy. 


What you will do:
  • Develop algorithms and ML solutions for traffic signs, traffic lights, road markings, and other traffic-control features, including projects with Computer Vision and Image Recognition.
  • Design and productionize solutions that extract reliable map information from diverse, large-scale and noisy real-world data sources, including car sensor data and unstructured information.
  • Improve how features are detected, positioned, and associated with the correct road/lane and driving direction.
  • Drive measurable improvements in recall, precision, and overall map quality against customer-facing targets.
  • Own components of production pipelines, from input data and feature extraction through evaluation and validated map output.
  • Solve complex problems involving geospatial geometry, map matching, computer vision, image recognition, noisy observations, ground-truth quality, and large-scale evaluation.
  • Run experiments, translate successful approaches into production solutions, and clearly document outcomes.
  • Use AI tools, such as Claude Code, to support problem solving, data analysis, implementation, and engineering productivity.
  • Mentor junior colleagues, provide insightful code reviews, and contribute to hiring. 

    • What you will need:
  • 4+ years of professional experience in Applied Science, Machine Learning, algorithm development, computer vision or related field.
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Geospatial Science, Statistics or another quantitative field. Master’s or PhD is a plus.
  • Strong fundamentals in algorithms and machine learning, including model development, evaluation, statistics and experimental design.
  • Proficiency in Python, an ML framework such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, and large-scale data processing tools such as Spark or Databricks.
  • Experience taking algorithms, ML models or data pipelines from experimentation into production.
  • Experience leading well-scoped technical projects and mentoring junior colleagues.
  • Ability to work across data, algorithms, modeling, ground truth and evaluation rather than operating within only one area of expertise.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to independently approach complex and ambiguous problems.
  • Proficient written and verbal communication skills in English.
  • You already live in the Netherlands. We cannot offer relocation for this role.

    A competitive compensation package, of course.  

    Time and resources to grow and develop, including a personal development budget and paid leave for learning days, as well as paid access to e-learning resources such as O’Reilly and LinkedIn Learning. 

    Time to support life outside of work, with enhanced parental leave plus paid leave to care for loved ones and volunteer in local communities.  

    Work flexibility, where TomTom’ers, in agreement with their manager and team, use both the office and home to focus, collaborate, learn and socialize.     Join annual events like our Hackathon and DevDays to bring your ideas to life with talented teammates from around the world. 

    Become a part of our inclusive global culture and have the chance to collaborate with a diverse community – we have over 80 nationalities at TomTom! 

    Find out more about our global benefits and enjoy additional local benefits tailored to your location. 


    Meet your team

    We’re Maps, a global team within TomTom’s Location Technology Products technical unit. Our team is driven to deliver the most up-to-date, accurate and detailed maps for hundreds of millions of users around the world. Every station we open is a tangible step in the transition away from fossil fuels. We are a listed company on Euronext Amsterdam, with a community of over 10,000 retail investors and a growing base of institutional funding partners. In 2025, we reported €122.4 million in charging revenue: a 47% year-on-year increase, exceeding €100 million in annual revenue for the first time. You know how to build a finance function that is both structured and able to move fast, effectively resolving scaling-bottlenecks along the way. You maintain strong financial discipline while enabling the continued investment needed to expand the charging network that supports our long-term vision. In this role, you oversee the full Finance domain, developing people and teams to the next phase. You act as a key financial voice within the Executive Team and Management Board. title: Manager Customer Data Engineering – Change & IT Customer Services
description: Wil jij bouwen aan de datafundering van de Customer Services-organisatie van morgen? Als Manager Customer Data Engineering ontwikkel je een ervaren engineeringteam door naar een strategisch Data Product Team. Je brengt data, technologie en business samen en zorgt voor betrouwbare, herleidbare en AI-ready dataproducten. Zo maak je met jouw leiderschap direct impact op besluitvorming, klantbediening én de verdere digitale ontwikkeling van Athora. Wat je over ons moet weten? Wij zijn Athora Netherlands, een verzekeringsbedrijf met de bekende merken Zwitserleven en Reaal. Wij houden ons voornamelijk bezig met pensioenen en levensverzekeringen op de Nederlandse markt. Dat doen wij als onderdeel van een Europese groep met vestigingen in Ierland, het Verenigd Koninkrijk, België, Duitsland en Italië. Wij zijn een sterk bedrijf met ruim één miljoen klanten en we willen de komende jaren doorgroeien tot een van de belangrijkste spelers in de snel veranderende pensioenmarkt. Daarom zoeken wij mensen die niet terugdeinzen voor verandering, die van aanpakken weten, die de ambitie hebben om resultaten neer te zetten en die daarom het beste uit zichzelf en hun team weten te halen. Slimmer samen, noemen wij dat. Wat ga je doen? De Manager Data Customer Engineering rapporteert aan de Director Change & IT Customer Services en geeft leiding aan een team van 10 data engineers en DevOps engineers. Het team is verantwoordelijk voor betrouwbare, herleidbare en bruikbare data voor interne bedrijfsvoering en sturing, operationele besluitvorming, externe verantwoordingsrapportages en toekomstige AI-toepassingen binnen het Customer Services en Commerce domein. De Manager Data Engineering is verantwoordelijk voor de doorontwikkeling van het huidige uitvoerende data- en rapportageteam naar een strategisch Data Product Team. De rol versterkt de data engineering capability binnen Customer Services door betrouwbare, herleidbare en AI-ready dataproducten te realiseren voor operationele sturing, besluitvorming, externe verantwoording en toekomstige data en AI-toepassingen. De manager borgt dat data een betrouwbare weergave vormt van businessprocessen en portalen, dat API's een robuuste en betrouwbare brug vormen tussen applicaties, en dat data-delivery plaatsvindt via Agile werkwijzen, schaalbare data engineering, gecontroleerde DevOps-processen en structurele datakwaliteitsborging. Belangrijkste verantwoordelijkheden: Ontwikkelen van het Data Engineering team naar een strategisch Data Product Team met end-to-end eigenaarschap voor betrouwbare en waardevolle dataproducten; Het doorvertalen van de Athora datastrategie binnen Customer Services, inclusief het verhogen van datamanagement maturity en het borgen van data lineage en traceerbaarheid. Hiertoe behoort ook de functionele sturing op de DQ processen, de functionele sturing richting de data stewards om de meting van en verbeteringen in de datakwaliteit vorm te geven; Leveren van betrouwbare, herleidbare, bruikbare en AI-ready data voor interne sturing, operationele besluitvorming, externe verantwoording en toekomstige AI-toepassingen; Borgen van datakwaliteit en een consistente datarepresentatie van businessprocessen, portalen, klantinteracties en operationele ketens binnen Customer Services. Wat vragen we van jou? WO werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur in informatica, data engineering, data science, informatiemanagement, bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare richting; 10-15 jaar ervaring met data engineering, IT delivery, DevOps, applicatieontwikkeling, dataplatformen of digitale transformatie, bij voorkeur in financiele dienstverlening; Ruime ervaring met het aansturen van data engineers, DevOps engineers, IT engineering professionals en/of multidisciplinaire data delivery teams; Ervaring met het realiseren van dataproducten, rapportageketens, data-integraties, operationele stuurinformatie en externe verantwoordingsrapportages; Sterke kennis van data engineering, datamodellering, datavisualisatie, data pipelines, metadata, lineage, datakwaliteit, DevOps, CI/CD, monitoring, cloud, API's, APIM, security-bydesign en beheerbaarheid; Ervaring met .NET-applicaties, integratiemodernisering, ESB-services, API-management, berichtenverkeer, datafundamenten en persoons- of klantadministraties; Ervaring met het vertalen van datastrategie, target architecture en businessprioriteiten naar concrete data roadmaps, technische keuzes en implementatieplannen; Kennis van AI-ready data, verantwoord datagebruik, datagovernance, automatisering en de toepassing van datafundamenten voor toekomstige AI-toepassingen; Ervaring met stakeholdermanagement richting business, reporting, IT, architectuur, data & AI, security, risk, compliance, leveranciers en senior management; Kennis van wet- en regelgeving, IT risk, privacy, security, datakwaliteit, DORA, EU AI Act en compliance-eisen binnen een gereguleerde omgeving; Ervaring met SAFe Agile standaarden en Agile data-delivery; Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift. Wij geloven dat onze mensen het verschil maken . Door de kennis en ervaring die zij meebrengen, maar ook door wie zij zijn. Naast de vier Athora kerncompetenties (moed, klantgerichtheid, samenwerken en resultaten leveren) zijn dit de vier belangrijkste competenties voor de Manager: Data Engineering: Data product leiderschap: ontwikkelt visie op betrouwbare, herleidbare en AI-ready dataproducten die waarde creëren voor business, reporting, compliance en toekomstige AI-toepassingen. Executiekracht: vertaalt datastrategie, architectuur en businessbehoeften naar roadmaps, dataproducten en voorspelbare Agile delivery. Engineering mindset: stimuleert vakmanschap, kwaliteit, ownership, DevOps, automatisering, beheerbaarheid en continue verbetering binnen data engineering. Datakwaliteit en control mindset: borgt dat data aantoonbaar betrouwbaar, traceerbaar, gecontroleerd en geschikt is voor besluitvorming, rapportage en verantwoording. Samenwerken met business, pensioenexperts, architectuur, data & AI, security, platformteams en leveranciers, inclusief contracteigenaarschap, contract- en leverancierssturing voor de leveranciers van relevante applicaties en oplossingen. Wat krijg je van ons? Je krijgt pakweg 900 collega’s die allemaal vinden dat ze bij een bijzonder bedrijf werken. Je krijgt de mogelijkheid om een belangrijke bijdrage te leveren aan het maatschappelijk relevante thema van pensioenen. Wij zorgen ervoor dat je pensioen goed geregeld is, zodat je zorgeloos kan genieten van je oude dag. Jij krijgt de kans om echt het verschil te maken als het gaat om duurzaamheid, omdat we in onze bedrijfsvoering en onze beleggingen al jaren de toon aangeven. Uiteraard krijg je een (flexibele) werkplek op ons kantoor in Amsterdam dat behoort tot de beste 7% van de wereld, echt waar. En omdat je ook regelmatig thuis zult werken, ontvang je een budget om je thuiswerkplek goed in te richten. In ruil voor jouw inzet, talent en vaardigheden krijg je naast je salaris plus een vakantietoeslag en een dertiende maand, 27 vakantiedagen (bij een contract van 36 uur) en een OV-kaart of reiskostenvergoeding voor de dagen dat je naar kantoor komt. En, niet onbelangrijk vinden wij, krijg je een goed opleidingsbudget, zodat je jezelf kunt blijven ontwikkelen. Zo krijg je de kans om door te groeien, binnen ons bedrijf of daarbuiten. Salaris per maand: Op basis van cao schaal 18 HAY is de range € 7.060,37 tot € 9.413,82 op basis van 36 uur. Enthousiast? Reageer dan snel via de sollicitatie button! De Manager Data Customer Engineering rapporteert aan de Director Change & IT Customer Services en geeft leiding aan een team van 10 data engineers en DevOps engineers. Het team is verantwoordelijk voor betrouwbare, herleidbare en bruikbare data voor interne
bedrijfsvoering en sturing, operationele besluitvorming, externe verantwoordingsrapportages en toekomstige AI-toepassingen binnen het Customer Services en Commerce domein. De Manager Data Engineering is verantwoordelijk voor de doorontwikkeling van het huidige
uitvoerende data- en rapportageteam naar een strategisch Data Product Team. De rol versterkt de data engineering capability binnen Customer Services door betrouwbare, herleidbare en AI-ready dataproducten te realiseren voor operationele sturing, besluitvorming, externe verantwoording en toekomstige data en AI-toepassingen. De manager borgt dat data een betrouwbare weergave vormt van businessprocessen en portalen, dat API's een robuuste en betrouwbare brug vormen tussen applicaties, en dat data-delivery plaatsvindt via Agile werkwijzen, schaalbare data engineering, gecontroleerde DevOps-processen en structurele datakwaliteitsborging.


Belangrijkste verantwoordelijkheden:

  • Ontwikkelen van het Data Engineering team naar een strategisch Data Product Team met end-to-end eigenaarschap voor betrouwbare en waardevolle dataproducten;

  • Het doorvertalen van de Athora datastrategie binnen Customer Services, inclusief het verhogen van datamanagement maturity en het borgen van data lineage en traceerbaarheid. Hiertoe behoort ook de functionele sturing op de DQ processen, de functionele sturing richting de data stewards om de meting van en verbeteringen in de datakwaliteit vorm te geven;

  • Leveren van betrouwbare, herleidbare, bruikbare en AI-ready data voor interne sturing, operationele besluitvorming, externe verantwoording en toekomstige AI-toepassingen;

  • Borgen van datakwaliteit en een consistente datarepresentatie van businessprocessen, portalen, klantinteracties en operationele ketens binnen Customer Services.


Wat vragen we van jou?

  • WO werk- en denkniveau, bij voorkeur in informatica, data engineering, data science, informatiemanagement, bedrijfskunde of een vergelijkbare richting;

  • 10-15 jaar ervaring met data engineering, IT delivery, DevOps, applicatieontwikkeling, dataplatformen of digitale transformatie, bij voorkeur in financiele dienstverlening;

  • Ruime ervaring met het aansturen van data engineers, DevOps engineers, IT engineering professionals en/of multidisciplinaire data delivery teams;

  • Ervaring met het realiseren van dataproducten, rapportageketens, data-integraties, operationele stuurinformatie en externe verantwoordingsrapportages;

  • Sterke kennis van data engineering, datamodellering, datavisualisatie, data pipelines, metadata, lineage, datakwaliteit, DevOps, CI/CD, monitoring, cloud, API's, APIM, security-bydesign en beheerbaarheid;

  • Ervaring met .NET-applicaties, integratiemodernisering, ESB-services, API-management, berichtenverkeer, datafundamenten en persoons- of klantadministraties;

  • Ervaring met het vertalen van datastrategie, target architecture en businessprioriteiten naar concrete data roadmaps, technische keuzes en implementatieplannen;

  • Kennis van AI-ready data, verantwoord datagebruik, datagovernance, automatisering en de toepassing van datafundamenten voor toekomstige AI-toepassingen;

  • Ervaring met stakeholdermanagement richting business, reporting, IT, architectuur, data & AI, security, risk, compliance, leveranciers en senior management;

Wij geloven dat onze mensen het verschil maken. Door de kennis en ervaring die zij meebrengen, maar ook door wie zij zijn. Naast de vier Athora kerncompetenties (moed, klantgerichtheid, samenwerken en resultaten leveren) zijn dit de vier belangrijkste competenties voor de Manager:

  • Executiekracht: vertaalt datastrategie, architectuur en businessbehoeften naar roadmaps, dataproducten en voorspelbare Agile delivery.

  • Engineering mindset: stimuleert vakmanschap, kwaliteit, ownership, DevOps, automatisering, beheerbaarheid en continue verbetering binnen data engineering.

  • Datakwaliteit en control mindset: borgt dat data aantoonbaar betrouwbaar, traceerbaar, gecontroleerd en geschikt is voor besluitvorming, rapportage en verantwoording. Samenwerken met business, pensioenexperts, architectuur, data & AI, security, platformteams en leveranciers, inclusief contracteigenaarschap, contract- en leverancierssturing voor de leveranciers van relevante applicaties en oplossingen.

title: AI Engineer l Young Talent Program
description: The rules of building are being rewritten. Come write them with us. Every few decades, the way companies are built gets reinvented from scratch. That is happening right now, and the people who learn to build in this new world first will define the next twenty years. Superstars are being made this year, not in ten. HelloPrint is a €100M+ e-commerce company serving businesses across Europe and the US. We are rebuilding the entire company as AI-first: our platform, customer service, operations, and how we design, price, sell, and deliver. Every piece of technology we run is being rewritten as we speak. We are doing it with a small, senior, very fast AI development team working shoulder to shoulder with our business leads. Now we are opening a handful of seats for young builders who want to grow faster than any graduate scheme, bootcamp, or big-tech ladder could ever let them. We don't care if you are 16, 25 or 30, whether you are self-taught, hacking in high school, or finishing a degree at TU Delft or TU/e—we care about what you have built and how fast you solve hard problems. The HelloPrint AI Residency is how you start. It is a permanent role from day one: your first year is a structured residency where you rotate across our most important AI projects, build alongside the team and learn at full speed. After that, you keep growing - in the direction where you have the most impact. What you will actually do: You will not get a training plan, a sandbox project or six months of shadowing. From week one, you build real things that real customers and colleagues use, on the projects that matter most to the company. You sit next to the founders, next to the engineers who are rebuilding our platform, and next to the business leads who own the outcomes. You get a lot of freedom and real responsibility, plus honest, direct guidance and feedback from people who have built this before. The kind of work you could be on in your first months: Agentic Commerce : making HelloPrint discoverable and orderable through AI assistants, so a customer can order business cards from inside a chat. AI Design Studio : letting customers create a print-ready design from a single sentence. AI-first customer service : replacing classic ticketing with agents that resolve questions, check artwork and handle orders end to end. Internal agent swarms : automating finance, purchasing, pricing and operations work that today still takes people hours. Whatever you spot next : if you see something we should build, you pitch it, and if it is good, you build it. We work with almost every modern framework and model, and we change our tools the moment something better appears. You will ship, measure, throw away and ship again - every week. Who you are: You are a builder before anything else . You have shipped things nobody asked you to build: an app, an agent, a bot, a tool your friends actually use, a side business, an open-source contribution, a weird experiment that taught you something. You probably have more GitHub commits, demos or deployed projects than most people twice your age. You are extremely curious and extremely critical. You read the new model release the day it drops and try it that evening. You question every assumption, including ours, and you can explain why. You are never satisfied with "it works" — you want to know why it works, and how it could be ten times better. You want to get better every single day, and you treat feedback as fuel rather than criticism. You take ownership: when something breaks, you fix it; when something is unclear, you go and find out. You have a solid grasp of backend and software fundamentals (Python, APIs, databases) or the raw learning capacity to pick them up in weeks. You will probably recognise yourself in most of this: You build with AI every day: Claude, Cursor, Lovable, agents, APIs, whatever gets you there fastest. You can show us concrete proof of work, not just tell us about it. You move fast without being sloppy, and you care about the details the customer sees. You are comfortable not knowing the answer, and you find it quickly. You communicate clearly in English, in writing and out loud. What we do not require: a degree, a minimum age, years of experience or a perfect CV. If you are still in school or university, we will make it work around that. What you get: The honest pitch: you will learn more here in one year than in five years almost anywhere else , because you will be building real systems for a real company that is reinventing itself, with the people who are leading that change. A contract from day one. The Residency is your first year at HelloPrint, not a trial period or an internship. Direct access to the founders and to a senior AI development team who review your work and push you. Ownership from day one : your name on projects that change how a €100M+ company runs. The best tools, no budget debates : the newest models, coding agents and frameworks, as soon as they are worth using. A growth path that follows your output, not your age : if you outgrow your role in six months, your role grows with you. A fast, flat, no-politics team in Rotterdam, with a hands-on culture and a high bar. Flexible set-up : full-time, or part-time alongside your studies. We care about what you deliver. Salary and contract are tailored to your situation and your level, and we pay properly for real talent. How to apply: Skip the cover letter. Show us what you have built. Send us three things: Your best project : a link to something you built: a live product, a repo, a demo video. Tell us in a few sentences what it does and what you would do differently now. Something you think is broken : one thing about HelloPrint (our website, our ordering flow, anything) that you would rebuild with AI, and how you would do it. A short intro : who you are and what you are obsessed with right now. Five sentences is plenty. What happens next: We read every application ourselves and reply within 5 days if you’re up to the next round A 15-minute call with one of our builders or founders about your projects. A Builders Day in our office: Together with other builders, you meet the team and if we have a click, you work on an assignment A conversation with the founders, and a decision the same day. We would rather hear from you too early than too late. If you are not sure you are ready, apply anyway;  your work will answer that question for us. It is a permanent role from day one: your first year is a structured residency where you rotate across our most important AI projects, build alongside the team and learn at full speed. After that, you keep growing - in the direction where you have the most impact.

What you will actually do:

You will not get a training plan, a sandbox project or six months of shadowing. From week one, you build real things that real customers and colleagues use, on the projects that matter most to the company. You sit next to the founders, next to the engineers who are rebuilding our platform, and next to the business leads who own the outcomes. You get a lot of freedom and real responsibility, plus honest, direct guidance and feedback from people who have built this before.

The kind of work you could be on in your first months:

  • Agentic Commerce: making HelloPrint discoverable and orderable through AI assistants, so a customer can order business cards from inside a chat.

  • AI Design Studio: letting customers create a print-ready design from a single sentence.

  • AI-first customer service: replacing classic ticketing with agents that resolve questions, check artwork and handle orders end to end.

  • Internal agent swarms: automating finance, purchasing, pricing and operations work that today still takes people hours.

  • Whatever you spot next: if you see something we should build, you pitch it, and if it is good, you build it.

We work with almost every modern framework and model, and we change our tools the moment something better appears. You will ship, measure, throw away and ship again - every week.


Who you are:

  • You are a builder before anything else. You have shipped things nobody asked you to build: an app, an agent, a bot, a tool your friends actually use, a side business, an open-source contribution, a weird experiment that taught you something. You probably have more GitHub commits, demos or deployed projects than most people twice your age.

  • You are extremely curious and extremely critical. You read the new model release the day it drops and try it that evening. You question every assumption, including ours, and you can explain why. You are never satisfied with "it works" — you want to know why it works, and how it could be ten times better.

  • You want to get better every single day, and you treat feedback as fuel rather than criticism. You take ownership: when something breaks, you fix it; when something is unclear, you go and find out.

  • You have a solid grasp of backend and software fundamentals (Python, APIs, databases) or the raw learning capacity to pick them up in weeks.

You will probably recognise yourself in most of this:

  • You build with AI every day: Claude, Cursor, Lovable, agents, APIs, whatever gets you there fastest.

  • You can show us concrete proof of work, not just tell us about it.

  • You move fast without being sloppy, and you care about the details the customer sees.

  • You are comfortable not knowing the answer, and you find it quickly.

  • You communicate clearly in English, in writing and out loud.


What we do not require: a degree, a minimum age, years of experience or a perfect CV. If you are still in school or university, we will make it work around that.

What you get:

The honest pitch: you will learn more here in one year than in five years almost anywhere else, because you will be building real systems for a real company that is reinventing itself, with the people who are leading that change.


A contract from day one. The Residency is your first year at HelloPrint, not a trial period or an internship.

  • Direct access to the founders and to a senior AI development team who review your work and push you.

  • Ownership from day one: your name on projects that change how a €100M+ company runs.

  • The best tools, no budget debates: the newest models, coding agents and frameworks, as soon as they are worth using.

  • A growth path that follows your output, not your age: if you outgrow your role in six months, your role grows with you.

  • A fast, flat, no-politics team in Rotterdam, with a hands-on culture and a high bar.

  • Flexible set-up: full-time, or part-time alongside your studies. We care about what you deliver.

Salary and contract are tailored to your situation and your level, and we pay properly for real talent.

How to apply:

Skip the cover letter. Show us what you have built.

Send us three things:

  1. Your best project: a link to something you built: a live product, a repo, a demo video. Tell us in a few sentences what it does and what you would do differently now.

  2. Something you think is broken: one thing about HelloPrint (our website, our ordering flow, anything) that you would rebuild with AI, and how you would do it.

  3. A short intro: who you are and what you are obsessed with right now. Five sentences is plenty.

What happens next:

  1. We read every application ourselves and reply within 5 days if you’re up to the next round

  2. A 15-minute call with one of our builders or founders about your projects.

  3. A Builders Day in our office: Together with other builders, you meet the team and if we have a click, you work on an assignment

  4. A conversation with the founders, and a decision the same day.

We would rather hear from you too early than too late. If you are not sure you are ready, apply anyway;  your work will answer that question for us. At HelloPrint, we believe diversity makes us better. We're building a workplace where everyone can be themselves, grow, and do their best work regardless of background, identity, or perspective. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

First and foremost, this is a hands-on selling role. You'll own the full sales cycle for Tellent HR (Manage and/or Grow), split roughly 80/20 between new business and expansion into our existing customer base. Inbound isn't going to be your main pipeline driver, so expect to spend around 50% of your time prospecting, against ambitious daily and weekly activity targets. Alongside that, you'll help us work out how we win in DACH: testing motions fast and doubling down on what drives revenue.

You'll work with a dedicated Product Marketing Manager and Customer Success Manager in the Tellent HR squad. CS capacity is limited, though, so you'll run deals independently, including demos and follow-through.

Your 12-Month Journey

  • First 3 months: Learn Tellent HR, our ideal customers and the competitive landscape in DACH. Build your first pipeline through outbound, establish a consistent daily activity rhythm, and close your first deals.

  • Within 6 months: Consistently hit your activity, pipeline and revenue targets, understand which sales motions work best in the DACH market, and feed insights back to Product Marketing and Product.

  • After 1 year: Be the go-to expert on selling Tellent HR in DACH, with a repeatable, data-backed playbook that others can pick up.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the full sales cycle, independently: Run 1–3 month, multi-stakeholder deals involving HR leaders, founders/CEOs and Finance, from first touch through to close and follow-through.

  • Hunt for new pipeline (around 50% of your time): Prospect by phone, email and LinkedIn, consistently hit your daily and weekly activity targets, and maintain 3–4x pipeline coverage. Partner, CS and marketing leads are a bonus, not the plan.

  • Drive expansion: Prospect into existing Tellent customers to cross-sell and upsell, e.g. Recruitee customers adding Tellent HR, or Manage customers adding Grow.

  • Sell on value: Run consultative discovery and tailored demos, position on business outcomes, and handle objections, including against key competitors (with support from PMM).

  • Manage deals with discipline: Use mutual action plans, keep HubSpot accurate (including SPICED), forecast reliably and disqualify early.

  • Test and build, alongside selling: Experiment with sales motions, sequences and verticals, help build the playbook with our PMM, and bring customer and competitive insights from the DACH market back to Product and Marketing.

What You Bring

  • Early-stage DNA: You've sold in a startup or early scale-up and built pipeline and processes where none existed. You know what it means to be an early sales hire.

  • Proven hunter: A track record of self-generating pipeline through outbound and consistently hitting ambitious activity targets. You genuinely enjoy picking up the phone and creating opportunities from scratch.

  • B2B SaaS sales experience: You've closed new business (ideally expansion too) as a fully autonomous AE in a startup or early scale-up, running 1–5 month, multi-stakeholder sales cycles. HR tech experience is a plus, not essential.

  • Self-sufficient and resilient: You don't wait for leads, support teams or perfect processes. You bounce back from rejection and stay disciplined through the ups and downs of building something new.

  • Consultative and data-driven: Strong discovery, demo and negotiation skills. You anchor on value before price and know your numbers (pipeline, conversion, win rate and cycle time).

  • Languages: Fluent English and native or fluent German are required. You'll be responsible for engaging customers and building relationships across the DACH market.

This role probably isn't for you if you want a structured environment with large support teams and steady inbound, or you're more excited by GTM strategy than by picking up the phone every day.

How We Measure Success

  • Closed-won revenue against target (primary KPI)

  • Daily and weekly outbound activity targets (key leading indicator, especially early on)

  • Self-generated pipeline and coverage

  • Win rate, deal velocity and forecast accuracy

  • Contributions to the playbook

What We Offer

  • Compensation: €55000–€70000 gross annual base salary, plus commission.

  • Ownership and impact: Real autonomy to shape the sales motion, playbook and market strategy for a growing product line.

  • Hybrid working: Work from our canal-side Amsterdam office 2–3 days per week.

  • International environment: Join a diverse and international team working across multiple markets.

  • Learning & Development: €1,500 annual learning budget and 2 dedicated learning days.

  • Pension & Wellness: Pension plan and wellness perks.

  • Time Off: 28 paid holiday days, plus 2 additional days in 2026.

  • Work from Anywhere: Work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks per year.

  • Commuting: Commuting and travel reimbursement.

  • Home Office: €200 home office budget and a work-from-home allowance.

  • Equipment: Apple MacBook and all the tools you need to succeed.

About Tellent

Tellent is a leading Talent Management Suite designed to empower HR & People teams across the entire employee journey. Our all-in-one platform combines an Applicant Tracking System (Tellent Recruitee), an intuitive HRIS (Tellent HR), and powerful Performance Management software (Tellent Grow).

With 250+ team members globally, 7,000+ customers in 100+ countries, and a growing ecosystem of 500+ partners, we help organizations attract, grow, and retain top talent — and we're just getting started.

AI in Our Recruitment Process

We use our internally developed AI tools to help streamline our recruitment process. However, technology never makes a decision. Every candidate is personally reviewed by our team. Your journey with us is guided by people, supported by tech. Curious about how it works? Read our AI Statement, check our Privacy Policy, or chat with us at

If you require accommodations or support during the recruitment process, please let us know — we're happy to help.
